prompt: Fill in the Knight and Dragon subclasses (a wounded dragon enrages) and write a duel that only ever talks to the abstract Creature type. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: hp is private and takeHit is final, so damage can only ever be applied one way and the rule that hp never drops below zero lives in a single method -- the subclasses supply numbers, not state changes. attackPower is abstract, so every creature must answer it, and the dragon's override computes its answer from the current hp instead of storing it, which is what makes the enrage rule impossible to get out of sync. duel and totalPower are written entirely against Creature, so dynamic dispatch picks the right attack and armour on every call without a single instanceof.
hints: The dragon's attackPower can ask getHp() each time it is called rather than keeping an enraged flag -- getHp() < 20 ? 24 : 12.
armour() already has a default of 0 in the base class, so each subclass just overrides it with its own protected int armour().
In duel, loop rounds 1..100: strike b, return if b is dead, then strike a, return if a is dead -- and fall out of the loop for the draw.
